title: Using gold nanobeacons as a theranostic technique to recognize, detect, and inhibit specific nucleic acids
protocol: In a fume hood, mix 3:1 concentrated HCl:HNO3 in an open and large container.
Immerse all the glassware (500 mL two-neck flask, magnetic stir bar, stopper, condenser, Erlenmeyer) in the freshly prepared aqua regia for at least 15 min.
Rinse the glassware with Millipore-filtered water.
Add 225 mL of 1 mM HAuCl4 into the rounded bottom two-neck flask.
Place the flask in the heating mantle and insert the stirrer.
Connect the condenser to one neck of the flask and place the stopper in the other neck.
Turn on the heating mantle to reflux while stirring.
Remove the stopper when the solution begins to reflux and swiftly add 25 mL of 38.8 mM sodium citrate.
Add the stopper back into the two-neck flask.
Observe a color change from pale yellow to deep red within approximately 1 minute.
Allow the system to continue refluxing for another 30 minutes with stirring.
Turn off heating and allow the system to cool to room temperature (23°C–25°C) protected from light.
Transfer the colloidal solution to a 250 mL amber flask with a ground glass cap.
Record a UV-Visible spectrum (300–900 nm) of the gold nanoparticles using a quartz cuvette.
Determine the concentration using the absorbance at the peak according to the Beer-Lambert law equation A = ε × l × c.
Consider any dilution performed prior to measurement.
Mix 41.7 mL of a 12 nM stock solution of citrate-capped gold nanoparticles (final concentration, 10 nM) with 150 μL of a 1 mg/mL stock solution of PEG (final concentration: 0.003 mg/mL).
Add DEPC-treated water to reach the desired final volume.
Incubate at room temperature (23°C–25°C) in a rotative shaker for 16 h.
Dissolve PEG powder stock in DMSO to intermediate concentrations.
Aliquot and store at -20°C.
Prepare a working solution of PEG by diluting an aliquot to 1 mg/mL in DEPC-treated water only at the time of functionalization.
Incubate gold nanoparticles with different amounts of PEG as needed.
Distribute the volume in centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 30 min at 4°C to remove excess PEG.
Collect 80%–90% of the supernatant and store it at 4°C.
Keep track of removed volume.
Resuspend the oily red deposition in DEPC-treated water after centrifugation.
Repeat step nine twice, collecting three supernatants in total.
Redisperse the final deposition in DEPC-treated water after the last centrifugation.
Collect and re-centrifuge the supernatant if it is not clear after initial centrifugation.
Record a UV-Visible spectrum of the PEGylated gold nanoparticles using a quartz cuvette.
Determine the concentration of PEGylated gold nanoparticles as described in step 7.
Prepare a calibration curve of PEG by mixing appropriate amounts of stock solution with phosphate buffer.
Add DEPC-treated water to each calibration curve mixture up to a final volume of 300 μL.
Mix, in triplicate, 200 μL of supernatants from steps 9 and 10 with 100 μL of phosphate buffer.
Prepare DTNB solution by dissolving the powder in phosphate buffer 0.5 M (pH=7).
Add 7 μL of freshly prepared 5 mg/mL DTNB to each mixture and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Observe a yellow color development, indicating free thiols presence in the supernatants.
Record the absorbance values at 412 nm.
Obtain an UV-Visible absorption spectrum from 290 to 600 nm for all samples.
Use the calibration curve to calculate the amount of free thiols in the supernatants.
Subtract the calculated free thiol value from the initial PEG amount added.
Determine the number of PEG chains attached to AuNPs using the equation y = mx + b, where y is absorbance at 412 nm, m is the slope, x is the concentration/amount of PEG, and b is the intercept.
Store nanoparticles functionalized with PEG at 4°C, protected from light, for 6 months.
Save an aliquot of the functionalized nanoparticles for later characterization.
Mix the lyophilized thiolated oligonucleotide with 1 mL of DEPC-treated water.
Collect an aliquot of 100 μL and store it at −20°C for later use.
Add 100 μL of 1 M Dithiothreitol (DTT) to the remaining 900 μL of oligonucleotide.
Incubate in a rotative shaker at room temperature for two hours or overnight at 4°C.
Extract one volume (500 μL) of thiol-modified oligonucleotide with two volumes (1,000 μL) of ethyl acetate.
Mix thoroughly.
Centrifuge at room temperature for 5 min at 20,000 × g.
Discard the organic phase (upper phase).
Repeat steps involving extraction and centrifugation twice more.
After the third extraction, purify the remaining aqueous phase using a desalting NAP-5 column according to manufacturer instructions.
Use 10 mM phosphate buffer (pH=8) as eluent.
Wash the column three times with 10 mM phosphate buffer (pH=8).
Add 500 μL of oligonucleotide solution.
Let the solution pass through the column – the oligonucleotides will be retained in the column.
Prepare a 1.5 mL Eppendorf for collection and add 1 mL of 10 mM phosphate buffer (pH=8) to release the oligonucleotide.
Quantify the purified oligonucleotide by UV-Visible spectroscopy using a Nanodrop.
Check the spectra for the existence of contaminations with DTT or ethyl acetate.
Mix the purified oligonucleotide with PEGylated AuNPs in a 1:100 AuNPs:oligonucleotide ratio.
Add ionic strength solution A to achieve a final concentration of 10 mM phosphate buffer (pH=8) and 0.01% (w/v) SDS.
Sonicate for 10 s and incubate for 20 min at room temperature in a rotative shaker.
Sequentially increase the ionic strength by adding volumes of ionic strength solution B up to a final concentration of 10 mM phosphate buffer (pH=8), 0.05 M NaCl, and 0.01% (w/v) SDS.
Sonicate for 10 seconds.
Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature (23°C–25°C) on a rotative shaker.
Place Ionic strength solutions A and B at room temperature until no precipitate is observed.
Warm the solution with agitation if any precipitate persists.
Repeat sonication step three times, each time adding final concentrations of 0.1 M, 0.2 M, and 0.3 M of NaCl.
Incubate for 16 hours at room temperature (23°C–25°C) on a rotative shaker, protected from light.
Centrifuge at 4°C for 20 minutes at 20,000 × g.
Collect 80%–90% of the supernatant and store it at 4°C.
Resuspend the deposition in 10 mM phosphate buffer pH=8.
Repeat step (resuspending the deposition) twice more.
After the final centrifugation, redisperse the deposition in 20%–30% of the initial volume in 10 mM phosphate buffer pH=8.
Be careful not to disturb the precipitate while removing the supernatant.
Record a UV-Visible spectrum of the Au-nanobeacons and determine the concentration as described in step 7.
Use at least 5 different concentrations to build the calibration curve.
Mix the appropriate amount of stock solution of fluorescent oligonucleotide with ionic strength solutions A and B to obtain a final volume of 100 μL.
Add all the calibration curve concentrations and 100 μL of each supernatant previously collected in triplicate to the wells of a microplate for fluorescence-based assays, 96-well.
Record the fluorescence emission of all the samples.
Use the equation of the calibration curve to determine the amount of fluorophore-labeled oligonucleotides present in each supernatant.
Subtract the determined amount from the initial amount added to step 20 to obtain the amount of oligonucleotides at the surface.
Ascertain the final AuNP:oligonucleotides ratio using this value.
Determine the hydrodynamic radius of Au-nanobeacons by Dynamic Light Scattering.
Measure the Zeta Potential to determine the surface charge of Au-nanobeacons.
Evaluate the size, morphology, and functionalization of Au-nanobeacons by staining with 2% phosphotungstic acid for 60–90 s and analyzing by TEM.
Mix 1 nM of Au-nanobeacons with complementary and non-complementary targets for a final volume of 100 μL.

Incubate the samples with different concentrations of target molecules in triplicate: a lower concentration than the nanobeacon’s, the same concentration as the nanobeacon’s, five times the nanobeacon’s concentration.
Add the samples to a black 96-well plate.
Record the emission (fluorescence intensity) of the Au-nanobeacons at 37°C every two minutes for 120 min using a plate reader.
Include controls by adding the same concentration of Au-nanobeacons alone, not mixed with complementary or non-complementary target.
Plot the results against the variable in study (i.e., amount of complementary/non-complementary target, time).
Incubate 1 nM of the Au-nanobeacons in phosphate buffer 10 mM (pH=8) at increasing temperatures ranging from 5°C to 80°C.
Record the emission every two minutes considering the excitation/emission wavelengths of the fluorophore in use.
Incubate 1 nM of the Au-nanobeacons in phosphate buffer 10 mM (pH=8) at decreasing temperatures ranging from 80°C to 5°C.
Record the emission every two minutes considering the excitation/emission wavelengths of the fluorophore in use.
Plot the resulting emission values against temperature.
Mix, in triplicate, 1 nM of Au-nanobeacons with different concentrations of glutathione (e.g., 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 5, 10 and 100 mM).
Transfer the samples to a microplate for fluorescence-based assays, 96-well.
Incubate the samples at 37°C for 120 min, acquiring emission data every 2 min.
Repeat the procedure with the same concentrations of DTT.
Plot the emission data results against time.
Prepare, in triplicate, 1 nM of Au-nanobeacons.
Transfer the samples to a microplate for fluorescence-based assays (100 μL/well).
Incubate the samples at different temperatures (e.g., 25, 30, 37, 40 and 45°C) for 60 min, acquiring emission data every 2 minutes.
Mix, in triplicate, 1 nM of Au-nanobeacons with 0.1 M potassium or sodium phosphate buffer solutions of different pHs (e.g., 5.8, 6.0, 6.2, 7.0, 7.4 and 8.0).
Transfer the samples to a microplate for fluorescence-based assays (100 μL/well).
Incubate the samples at 37°C for 120 min, acquiring emission data every 2 minutes.
Mix, in triplicate, 1 nM of Au-nanobeacons with different concentrations of RNAse or DNAse.
Transfer the samples to a microplate for fluorescence-based assays (96-well, 100 μL/well).
Incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Acquire emission data every minute.
Plot the emission data results against time.
Detach cells with trypsin-EDTA 1× in the day before incubation with antisense Au-nanobeacon.
Resuspend detached cells in complete growth medium and pellet by centrifugation at 250×g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in 10 mL of complete growth medium.
Calculate the amount of cell suspension needed for seeding 1×10^5 cells/well.
Seed 1×10^5 cells per well in a 24-well plate using 500 μL of appropriate complete growth medium.
Incubate at 37°C in a humidified 5% CO2 atmosphere for 24 h.
Check cell density using an inverted optical microscope to ensure cells are 70%-80% confluent.
Adjust the seeding density according to the type of cells used, as different cells have varying growth rates.
For experiments requiring confocal microscopy, seed cells on sterile glass slides placed at the bottom of the wells.
Use round coverslips with a diameter of 12 mm and thickness less than 1.5 mm for 24-well plates if necessary.
Pre-treat coverslips with gelatin (2% w/v in water) for 15 min at 37°C if cells do not adhere directly to the slides.
Alternatively, use confocal dishes instead of glass slides on 24-well plates to avoid breakage during removal.
Remove the medium of each well.
Add Au-nanobeacons targeting MRP1 in complete growth medium to a final volume of 500 μL/well.
Mix well to ensure even distribution of nanoparticles in the well.
Incubate at 37°C in a humidified 5% CO2 atmosphere for 24 h.
Collect and lyse cells after 24 h for total RNA extraction using PureLink™ RNA Mini Kit.
Prepare samples for cDNA conversion using High-Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit with RNase Inhibitor.
Use cDNA samples to perform RT-qPCR using TaqMan™ Fast Advanced Master Mix and TaqMan probes for the target mRNA and an endogenous control like GAPDH.
Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for performing RT-qPCR.
Evaluate the expression against the endogenous control.
Calculate the fold-change relative to non-treated cells.
After 24 hours, remove the growth medium from the cells.
Wash cells with PBS 1×.
Fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS 1× for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Mount the coverslip containing fixed cells on a slide using ProLong® Gold Antifade Reagent with DAPI for nuclear staining.
Image the cells on a fluorescence or confocal microscope taking into account the excitation/emission wavelengths of the dyes used and of the fluorophore in the Au-nanobeacons.
Plate cells at a density of 1×10^5 cells/well in 24-well plates.
Grow cells to achieve 70%–80% confluence before incubation with Au-nanobeacons.
Incubate cells in complete medium.
Add 10, 30 and 50 nM of Anti-miR Au-nanobeacons to cells.
Incubate for 24, 48 and 72 hours.
Wash cells with PBS 1× after incubation.
Lysate the cells.
Extract total RNA from lysed cells.
Prepare samples for fluorescence/confocal microscopy.
Quantitative assessment of miR-21 silencing in HCT-116 cells induced by 10, 30, and 50 nM Anti-miR Au-nanobeacon for 24, 48, and 72 hours using b-actin as a reference.
Confirm miR-21 silencing by RT-PCR followed by agarose gel electrophoresis.
Conduct qRT-PCR analysis of the assay versus control normalized for b-actin expression under the same conditions.
Normalize endogenous control for miRNA expression, ideally using RN6UB.
